author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A planned Monday meeting between Iran and Gulf states in Oman is expected to cover the Strait of Hormuz but is unlikely to produce a signed agreement, a senior Iranian official told Reuters. The assessment tempers expectations around talks focused on one of the world’s most consequential shipping routes.

Iran has spent months negotiating with Oman and says it plans to attend the gathering. Oman has not formally announced the meeting, while other invited governments have remained largely silent; Bahrain has said it will not participate. Tehran has sought fees from vessels using the strait, a proposal Oman rejects, leaving a central point of disagreement unresolved before delegates meet.

Roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies moved through Hormuz before the war that began in February, making any change in access important to energy markets and shipping costs. Oil prices surged during the past week as regional risks intensified. The official’s comments indicate that Monday may function as a negotiating step rather than a deadline. Confirmation of attendance, the meeting’s agenda and any practical navigation arrangements remain the key developments to watch.
dek: A senior Iranian official described Monday’s Oman meeting as a negotiating step, with major disagreements over the strategic waterway unresolved.
headline: Iran says Oman talks unlikely to produce signed Hormuz deal
